title: My love for incremental/idle games made me create one of my own called Graveharvest
author: Traditional_Solid_73
selftext:
I want to share the game I have been working on since late July. It is a free beta, it still has rough edges, and I am looking for playtesters and honest feedback.

Graveharvest is a dark pixel-art idle game. You are a necromancer under a blood moon, cutting down the Living as they cross the field, or letting the Reaping do it for you. You raise the dead as Vassals who gather Souls every second, buy Rites that make every kill worth more, and when prices outrun your harvest you take the Long Death: the life ends, the Ichor you earned stays, and the covenants it buys make the next life climb faster. It is a long game, made to sit in the background and be come back to. Finishing it takes months, not an evening.

AI has been a life changer for me as a solo dev. I have always had more game ideas than time, and spending years on a single game was never something I could afford. Now I write the design, break it into tasks, and hand them to Claude. It feels like running a small team: a stronger model plans and reviews, a cheaper one writes the code from tightly scoped briefs, and I make every design call and play every build. The engine is Godot 4.

It is still not easy. There are always bugs, and almost everything needs a manual pass. Two things kept the project from falling apart as it grew: over 1,600 automated tests that have to pass before anything ships, and a simulation kept separate from the visuals, so the economy can be tested and balanced without opening the game. I also learned that the AI does far better with something to look at. Even a rough mock-up beats a paragraph of description. Characters, icons and music come from asset packs (credited in the game), and some of the ground art was generated with Gemini. It is hard to believe how much game there is after less than four months.

I honestly do not understand all the hate AI-assisted games get. I think transparency matters, so I am open about how this one is made, and I will say so on the store page if it goes to Steam. But seeing the reaction some AI-assisted games get, I do have doubts about that. How do other devs here handle it?

What I would most like to hear about the game:

\- the first ten minutes: is it clear what to do without being told?

\- the pacing and the prices, early on and after your first Long Death

\- any bug you hit, and anything that feels unpolished

It runs in the browser, and there is a Windows download too. It asks once whether it may share anonymous play statistics; that is off unless you say yes.

I look forward to your constructive criticism!

[https://jbi2109.itch.io/graveharvest](https://jbi2109.itch.io/graveharvest)
